info.title: Atlas API
info.description:
The Atlas API lets your systems add the merchants G2 monitors for you and pull back what
G2 finds: findings and their risk, reports and comments. Get an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials
token; every endpoint except health needs it. Add and update merchants and their stores under
/api/v1/merchants. Call GET /api/v1/portfolios to find your portfolio ids; a merchant's review
decision, findings, snoozes and comments, and the reports, are under
/api/v1/portfolios/{portfolioId}/... Set a finding's status with PATCH
/api/v1/findings/{findingId}/status.

**Polling.** Long-running work (CSV reports) returns PENDING; poll the list endpoint until it is
READY.

**Reviewing a merchant.** Record your decision with PATCH
/api/v1/portfolios/{portfolioId}/merchants/{merchantId}, sending merchantStatus. TERMINATED also
cancels the merchant's snoozes in that portfolio and leaves its finding statuses as they are. It
does not stop scans: to stop scanning the merchant, send monitoringStatus PAUSED in the same call
or a later one. A terminated merchant's status can no longer be changed.

**Versioning.** Every endpoint is under /api/v1.

**Request id.** Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it when contacting
support. A value sent by the client is ignored.

**Timeouts.** Some requests take longer than others, such as creating a merchant with many
stores. Set the client timeout to at least 60 seconds.

**Rate limits.** Requests over the limit get 429. Wait, then retry with exponential backoff.

**Retries.** 502 and 503 are safe to retry for reads. Retrying a merchant create that already
succeeded returns 409 MERCHANT_ALREADY_EXISTS.

**Availability.** `GET /api/v1/health` needs no token and returns UP or DOWN. It checks only that
the API itself is running, not the services behind it, so it can be UP while a call fails with 502
or 503. Retry a failed call with backoff; DOWN or no answer means the API itself is unavailable.

tags.name: Comments
tags.description:
Comments on merchants and findings, shared with Atlas UI users.

Finding comments belong to the finding's store and category. Findings with the same
store and category share a comment list; each redirect finding has its own list.
The finding ID in the URL selects that list.

Edit and delete requests do not accept a version or ETag. A 409 means another change
conflicted while the request was being processed; your change was not applied.
Review the latest comment before deciding on another change.

get.description: Returns a page of merchants. Omit the filters to list all merchants in your account. clientMerchantKey matches exactly and case-sensitively; URL-encode the value. portfolioId restricts results to merchants in that portfolio. When nextCursor is absent, there are no more results.

patch.summary: Set a merchant's review and monitoring status
patch.description: Changes the merchant's status in this portfolio. Send merchantStatus, monitoringStatus or both; a field you leave out is unchanged. Both fields are applied in one atomic update: if the request fails, neither field changes. Each field keeps its own effects, described on the field: TERMINATED cancels the merchant's snoozes in this portfolio, and PAUSED stops monitoring scans. Neither field changes the other.

patch.description: Records your decision on one finding using only its ID. TO_REVIEW and IN_PROGRESS leave the finding's risk as the scan set it. RISK confirms the finding: it keeps counting toward the merchant's risk at the severity the scan gave it, never higher. NO_RISK dismisses it and takes it out of the merchant's risk. The merchant's risk is recalculated shortly after the call, not in its response. Each finding is separate: other findings of the same category on the store keep their own status.

post.summary: Snooze a category on a store, or a whole store
post.description: Marks a category on a store (FINDING) or a whole store (URL) as snoozed until an end date, at most 12 months away, so you can leave it out of your review queue. A snooze does not change risk, stop scans or hide findings. For FINDING, send storeId and categoryId. The server selects a finding of that category on the store. When a snooze ends or is cancelled, the covered findings go back to TO_REVIEW, replacing any status you set: the source finding for FINDING, every finding on the store for URL. A URL snooze is cancelled early if a scan finds a new category on the store. Snooze must be enabled for the portfolio by G2; otherwise 403.

level.description: FINDING snoozes one category on one store: every finding of categoryId on storeId. A store and category can have one active snooze; a second gets 409. URL snoozes every finding on the store until a scan finds a new category there.

storeId.description: The storeId of the finding or store to snooze

categoryId.description: Required for FINDING: the category to snooze on storeId. The server selects a finding of this category on the store.

categoryIds.description: URL only, optional: the categories the store has now. When omitted or empty, the categories of the store's current findings are used. If a later scan finds any other category, the snooze is cancelled.

durationPreset.description: How long the snooze lasts. The presets count calendar months from now; CUSTOM ends at wakeDate, which must be in the future and at most 12 months away.

wakeDate.description: When the snooze ends; required with durationPreset CUSTOM and ignored otherwise

reason.description: Why it is snoozed; shown to everyone reviewing the merchant

Snooze.description: An active snooze on a finding category or a store

examples.reason: Reviewed with the merchant, casino page removed

level.description: FINDING: one category on one store is snoozed. URL: the whole store is snoozed.

findingId.description: The finding that the server selected for this snooze. When a FINDING snooze ends or is cancelled, only this finding goes back to TO_REVIEW.

categoryId.description: The snoozed category; FINDING snoozes only

categoryIds.description: Categories on the store when a URL snooze was set. If a later scan finds any other category, the snooze is cancelled. Empty for FINDING snoozes.

reason.description: Why it was snoozed; shown to everyone reviewing the merchant

createdBy.description: Identity of the user or API client that created the snooze

wakeDate.description: When the snooze ends and the covered findings go back to TO_REVIEW

merchantStatus.description: Your review decision for the merchant in this portfolio: TO_REVIEW (not reviewed yet), IN_PROCESS (being reviewed), APPROVED, REJECTED or TERMINATED. Approve or reject a merchant after Onboarding or after Monitoring. REJECTED does not change monitoringStatus. TERMINATED also cancels the merchant's snoozes in this portfolio; finding statuses and monitoringStatus are left as they are. Once TERMINATED, merchantStatus cannot be changed: sending it returns 409, as does sending the status the merchant already has.

monitoringStatus.description: Whether G2 keeps scanning the merchant in this portfolio: ACTIVE or PAUSED. PAUSED stops monitoring scans until it is set back to ACTIVE; merchantStatus, findings and snoozes are left as they are. Sending the status the merchant already has changes nothing.

url.description: The address that was scanned when the finding was raised: the store's URL or another page of the same store, such as the page it redirects to. Use it as the link a reviewer opens to check the finding.

redirectedUrl.description: Redirect (61) findings only: the address the store redirects to. Absent on other findings, and on Redirect findings whose evidence does not name an address.

categoryId.description: What kind of issue this is. Findings of the same category on the same store are reviewed as one item in Atlas UI. mccDetection tells MCC detections apart from other findings.

categoryName.description: Readable name of the category, for display

status.description: Your review decision on this finding. It stays TO_REVIEW until someone sets it. It returns to TO_REVIEW when a FINDING snooze that selected it ends or is cancelled. A URL snooze on its store also resets it when it ends or is cancelled.

riskSeverity.description: How severe this finding is: the category's severity for your account, or NO_RISK once the finding is dismissed. Use it to prioritise review.

evidenceUrl.description: The page the evidence was seen on, as the scanner reported it. Usually a full URL on the scanned store, but it can be a bare host or N/A, so show it as text and use url as the link.

evidenceText.description: What the scanner found, as text to show a reviewer. Its form depends on the category: a JSON object (for example the detected email or phone in raw_entity, or keyword counts), an address for Online (59) and Redirect (61), or a short label such as UNSUPPORTED DOMAIN. Show it as text; its JSON keys are not part of the contract.

lastModifyDate.description: When a scan last wrote this finding (UTC). Setting a status does not change it.

snooze.description: The active snooze covering this finding; absent when not snoozed. A snoozed finding still counts toward the merchant's risk.

ignored.description: True when the store does not count toward the merchant's risk. Only stores G2 found connected to the merchant can be ignored: your portfolio is set to leave connected stores out of the risk, or a reviewer excluded the store in Atlas UI. Read-only; you can usually skip these findings.

mccDetection.description: True when the finding is an MCC detection: its category is a merchant category code the scan matched to the store's business, not an issue found on the store. False for every other finding.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; absent when there are no more results

snoozeId.description: ID of the snooze; use it to change or cancel the snooze

level.description: FINDING: this category on this store is snoozed. URL: the whole store is snoozed.

wakeDate.description: When the snooze ends; the findings then go back to TO_REVIEW.

Problem.description: The error body the API returns, as RFC 9457 problem details in application/problem+json. Branch on status and code, not on title or detail.

examples.title: Not Found
examples.detail: No such resource under this account

title.description: The HTTP reason phrase; do not branch on it

status.description: Same as the HTTP status; branch on this

detail.description: Human-readable reason for logs and support; the wording can change

instance.description: Request path that caused the problem

code.description: Machine-readable reason; branch on it, not on detail. One of INVALID_REQUEST (400), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), FORBIDDEN (403), NOT_FOUND (404), CONFLICT (409), RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500), BAD_GATEWAY (502), SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (503), or MERCHANT_ALREADY_EXISTS (409 when creating a merchant whose clientMerchantKey is taken). New values may be added; when code is absent or unknown, branch on status

categoryTypeName.description: Category type name, for example Content or Availability

findingId.description: The finding's identifier in the API, for status, comment and snooze calls

url.description: Page the finding was detected on

evidenceText.description: The evidence as a JSON string; its fields are not a stable contract, so show it, do not parse it

risk.description: Risk severity of the finding; riskSeverity in the API

CallbackMcc.description: Comparison of the reported MCC with the MCCs detected on the store

detected.description: MCCs detected on the store; absent when none were

codeName.description: Code and name, for example 5993 - Cigar Stores And Stands

CallbackMccDetection.description: A merchant category code detected on the store

groupId.description: Group the comparison is made in

findingId.description: The finding the code was detected from

match.description: Whether it matches the reported code; absent when none was reported

X-Request-Id.description: Identifier of this request. Quote it when contacting support.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow. Request an access token from the token URL with your client id, client secret and audience https://mlrc-external-api.everc.com/ (also published as x-audience), then send it as Authorization: Bearer. G2 links the client to your account when it sets the client up; a token without that link gets 403.

post.description:
After a scan of a store, G2 POSTs this to your HTTPS endpoint, once G2 switches callbacks on for your account. A callback is a signal: read the merchant's findings from the API and act on them there.

Answer with any 2xx within 1-2 seconds; the hard limit is 5 seconds. A timeout, 429 or 5xx is retried with backoff for up to 24 hours; other 4xx are not retried. Delivery is at least once and in no particular order, so drop duplicates by callbackId. Each callback carries an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials token that G2 gets from your token URL, as Authorization: Bearer. When a product on the portfolio has graphEnabled on, its scans also find stores connected to the merchant's stores, and each connected store gets callbacks too. Those callbacks have no mcc block.
